title: Table 5.07 Summary of the main features of Muir–Torre syndrome
source: Maya Eiger-Moscovich
tablehtml:
Feature

Syndrome characteristics

Syndrome MIM number(s)

158320

Associated malignant tumours

Lynch syndrome–associated visceral malignancies, including tumours of the colorectum, endometrium, stomach, small bowel, ovary, gallbladder, hepatobiliary tract, pancreas, urinary tract, kidney, brain, and prostate; seldom associated with malignant cutaneous sebaceous lesions, i.e. sebaceous carcinoma

Associated benign tumours

Cutaneous lesions including well-differentiated sebaceous neoplasms, mainly sebaceous adenoma, but also sebaceoma (but not sebaceous hyperplasia) and keratoacanthoma

Cancer-related inheritance

Autosomal dominant

Chromosome location

The primary cause of Muir–Torre syndrome is a germline pathogenic variant affecting a DNA mismatch repair gene:

·   MLH1 (3p22.2)

·   MSH2 (2p21)

·   MSH6 (2p16.3, only 300 kb from MSH2)

·   PMS2 (7p22.1)

Some individuals have mutations involving adjacent genes, such as EPCAM (2p21), which affects the neighbouring MSH2 gene, or LRRFIP2 (3p22.2), which affects MLH1

The phenotype can also be seen in patients with autosomal recessive MUTYH (1p34.1)-associated adenomatous polyposis (familial adenomatous polyposis 2; MIM number: 608456)

Protein product–associated pathway

DNA mismatch repair
